subject.title: San Jose Unified School District Board, Trustee Area 2

text: Public School Teacher

I'm running to be your school board member for San Jose Unified School District because I know what our public schools need in order for every student to succeed. As a public school teacher for 12 years, I've gained experience and learned how to provide what schools need to be for all students to be successful!

As a Special Education Teacher for 12 years, I've advocated for students and educators to make our schools the best places of learning they can be. I've seen what happens when students get consistency, dedicated services for every need, and robust programming: they grow into their full potential. That's the future I'm running for: a district where every dollar and every decision moves us closer to welcoming schools where all our kids can learn and feel seen.

Families in Trustee Area 2 believe their children can thrive. What they want are neighborhood schools they can count on to serve their children's needs. I will be a board member who works alongside educators to build those schools.

My lived experience as a Black and Mexican woman who grew up with very little and made the most of every opportunity taught me that all students deserve a real shot at success. I will keep Black, brown, disabled, and low-income students at the heart of the district's decisions.

As an active union member, I've served as a Representative in multiple roles, and I now serve as my teacher union's Equity Chair. In that work, I collaborate with teachers and administrators to identify problems, research solutions, and implement change with an equitable approach to education. As your board member, I'll rebuild trust through shared responsibility with educators and families, listening, communicating openly, and responding to what students actually need based on my many years of experience as an educator. I graciously ask that you vote Tomara Hall for San Jose Unified School District, Trustee Area 2.
Learn more at www.VoteTomaraHall.com

Endorsed by: Santa Clara County Assessor Neysa Fligor, SCC Board of Supervisors President Susan Ellenberg, Board of Equalization Chair Sally Lieber, SCCBOE Trustee Raeena Lari, Silicon Valley Young Democrats and many community leaders, educators and parents.

text: Student Services Professional

I am a parent and former president for the Parent Teacher Organization of San Jose Unified's largest elementary school. I have worked within our community to increase access to after school programming, support the safety of students walking and biking to schools, and create systems to better support our classroom teachers.

Fostering a culture of collaboration and communication begins with the district, from school board members to administrators and teachers. Crucially, parents need to be involved in their children's education. Historically the district has failed to meaningfully engage, as they did in the recent closure of five schools, and the community believes that their input and engagement is not valued. We can do better for all students in our district. The district should provide the tools and leadership to help parents participate in their students' success.

Our schools should be appropriately staffed. Every kindergarten classroom needs support staff to manage behaviors so our teachers can teach. Inconsistent staffing of substitute teaching positions leaves gaps in our students' education and school safety plans.

We need to carefully evaluate the use of technology in our classrooms. For our youngest students, we should consider if any technology has a place in the classroom. For our older students, we should ensure that the software we use can provide results consistent with other measures of achievement. Our district needs a policy on the use of AI that ensures that students, teachers, and staff are meaningfully engaging with content.

Our curriculum needs to provide appropriate instruction for all students. Expecting teachers to provide differentiation in the classroom with the resources they currently have is unreasonable. Each student should be provided an opportunity to grow their abilities, and curriculum and classroom resources should reflect that goal.

Our district needs leadership. I have served as PTO president, substitute teacher across several SJUSD schools, Girl Scout troop leader to over forty girls, and executive treasurer for a nonprofit serving children and their families in Santa Clara County. Professionally, I work in student services for universities helping implement educational programs. I have the skills and commitment to move our district forward.
CarsonforSJUSD.com

text: Governing Board Member

I moved to San José to teach kindergarten. Nearly fifteen years later, I am running for re-election to the San José Unified School District Board of Education because I still believe what I believed in that classroom: every child deserves a world-class education, including my daughters, who attend our neighborhood public school. We have made real progress these last four years, but there is more work to do for our students, families, and community.

My teaching experience took me further than I expected. I went from my own students to classrooms nationwide, coaching teachers in mathematics and literacy. Most recently, I served as executive director of an education policy nonprofit that trains school leaders across California.
As your trustee these last four years, I put my Certificate in Education Finance, my experience as a teacher, and a proven track record to work. During my term, we:
Partnered with Stanford and SJSU to secure free student resources and staff training.
Won a raise for teachers and staff, and launched a workforce housing initiative so they can afford to live in the community they serve.
Secured $800+ million in funding for school facility upgrades.
Earned the district's highest credit rating, saving taxpayers millions of dollars.

With another four years, I will keep building partnerships that invest in student safety, academics, STEM, and extracurriculars. I will make sure students are ready to compete in an economy reshaped by AI, whether they choose college, a trade, or starting their own business. I will continue protecting the mental health resources our students rely on and the policies that make every student welcome on campus—even as those resources and policies are threatened by our current political climate. Now more than ever, this board needs a proven policymaker and an experienced educator who keeps the focus on students, not politics.

This work is personal. My daughters attend our neighborhood public school, so every vote I take on this board is a vote about their education and your child's. I want for every student in Area 2 what I want for them—educators who are supported, campuses that are safe, and a diploma that opens doors. I humbly ask for your vote this November for SJUSD Area 2 Trustee. Learn more at www.votejosemagana.com
